content.text: I want to build a small Linux desktop tool that converts tables in PDFs into clean Excel or CSV files. I regularly receive bank statements, brokerage notes, and corporate reports; the current tools either scramble the columns or upload sensitive documents to a server. It should work fully offline on Debian, handle both text-based PDFs and scanned pages, let me preview the detected table before export, and preserve numbers and dates well enough for manual checking in LibreOffice Calc. I am considering adding this to an existing open-source PDF utility. Is it worth building?

content.text: Recommendation: Adapt. This is worth pursuing as a focused Debian-first offline review workflow, but not as a general-purpose PDF-to-Excel engine from scratch. Reuse Tabula/Camelot/pdfplumber for text geometry, Tesseract/OCRmyPDF or Docling/Table Transformer for scans, and add the missing product layer: region selection, preview, source-cell highlighting, confidence flags, manual correction, typed XLSX/CSV export, raw text/provenance, and explicit failure checks. Tabula already provides local Linux preview and CSV/Excel but is text-only and its site release is from 2018. Excalibur is a local Camelot UI but text-only. Current Camelot supports optional ML/OCR and quality metrics, while OCRmyPDF supplies only the OCR layer. Docling can run offline after model artifacts are cached and exports detected tables through pandas, but it lacks the requested desktop review/export flow. openstan proves a Debian/offline finance workflow can be useful, but is bank-specific; PDFcsv and PDF Workbench show narrow implementations; Anchor is the closest full product match but publishes Windows/macOS support only, is beta, uses an Elastic License 2.0 release, and needs a large first-run model download. The TabSniper paper shows why universal accuracy is hard: bank layouts vary, statements are long multi-page dense multi-line tables, and tilted scans can still fail. Calc warns that CSV dates and decimals are locale-sensitive, so export typed XLSX cells with explicit formats and preserve the raw recognized string beside each normalized value. Integrate through a host-neutral local worker with an optional action in a maintained GTK/Java PDF utility such as PDF Arranger or PDFsam, after verifying an extension point. Pilot on redacted text/scanned/mixed documents from two or three target banks or brokerages plus one corporate-report family; require no silent row drops, source provenance for every exported cell, and reconciliation checks where available. Use existing software if the need is occasional clean text-PDF extraction; stop or narrow the build if the requirement expands to arbitrary layouts, handwriting, many languages, or guaranteed accounting-grade accuracy on unseen documents.
